title: Gluten-Free Board
seo_title: Gluten-Free Charcuterie Board for 8–12: Safe Shopping List
description: A gluten-free charcuterie board for 8–12: aged cheddar, Manchego, brie, Parmigiano, prosciutto, salami, GF crackers, fruit and labeled condiments.
hook: Zero gluten, full flavor: a board where the cheese and meat are naturally safe and the care goes into the crackers and the knives.
why: Natural, aged cheese contains no gluten, and neither does prosciutto, so the risk on a board sits in the crackers, some processed meats and cross-contact. That's why this board uses only gluten-free crackers and checks every label on the salami, pepperoni, jam and mustard.
For guests with celiac disease, a few crumbs from a shared knife are enough to matter. Use a clean board and dedicated knives, and label it gluten-free so guests can eat without asking.

timeline.what: Check every label for gluten; take out the cheeses.
Set a clean board and clean knives aside for the GF board.
Place the cheeses and fill the condiment bowls.
Add the meats, fruit, crackers and nuts.
Label the board gluten-free and serve.

faq.a: Natural cheese and most cured whole-muscle meats like prosciutto are gluten-free. Some salami, pepperoni, jams and mustards can contain gluten, and crackers usually do, so check labels.
Rice crackers, seed crackers, corn tortilla chips, plain potato chips and certified gluten-free crackers.
Use a clean board and knives that haven't touched bread, keep gluten-containing crackers off the board entirely, and serve the GF board first.
